Listen to this article Share The Kogi State Police Command has arrested eight suspected cultists in Itobe, Ofu Local Government Area and three members of an ATM card-swapping fraud syndicate in Idah on the Eastern part of the State. Naziru Bello Kankarofi, Kogi State Commissioner of Police, stated this on Wednesday during the Parade and Press Conference held at the Command’s Headquarters in Lokoja, Kogi State Capital. Kankarofi said, “On 17 October 2026, at about 5:45 p.m., operatives of the Itobe Division, working with local auxiliary forces and community leaders, acted on credible intelligence and raided a location behind Government Secondary School, Itobe, leading to the arrest of eight male suspects: Mutari Ahmed, 26; Mohammed Tairu, 21; Audu Moses Yahaya, 27; Peter Vincent, 28; Progress Aminu, 21; Wisdom Friday, 21; Gabriel Enema, 22; and a 14-year-old boy. Items recovered included two TVS motorcycles, an axe and a cutlass”. He explained that Preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects had gathered to appoint a leader for a local cult group. “Some admitted membership of the Aro-Baga Vikings and Aiye confraternities and provided information on other persons connected to their activities,” Kankarofi noted. He noted that the arrests are significant in view of intelligence regarding planned violent clashes between rival cult groups in Itobe and Ejule communities, as he attributed it to longstanding rivalries, territorial disputes and retaliatory attacks, adding that the Command is also addressing reprisal threats against security personnel and facilities, with measures strengthened to prevent violence, protect residents and commuters, and maintain security in the area. The commissioner equally pointed out that the case had been transferred to the Violent Crime Response Unit for further investigation, including efforts to apprehend fleeing suspects, identify accomplices and establish the full extent of the groups’ activities. He pointed out that the Nigeria Police Force has no friendly, supportive or compromising relationship with cultists, secret confraternities or any criminal elements. He said that residents of Itobe, Ejule and neighbouring communities, as well as commuters along the Itobe–Anyigba Road, are advised to remain vigilant, continue their lawful activities without panic, and report suspicion criminal cult activities should desist immediately. The Police will continue to act on credible intelligence and take lawful action against anyone found culpable,” he said. CP Bello Kankarofi also said, “On 20 October 2026, at about 9:30 a.m., Police operatives arrested three suspects in Idah for criminal conspiracy, fraudulent banking activities and ATM card swapping. They are Philip Akiola, 50; Ojo Thomas, 56; and Abdulrauf Suleiman, 48.” The arrests followed sustained surveillance initiated after a complaint on 19 May 2026, in which the victim reported that his ATM card had been swapped, resulting in the loss of N1.5 million from his account. “The operation led to the recovery of 59 ATM cards belonging to different banks and a vehicle used by the syndicate. Preliminary investigations indicate that the syndicate targets unsuspecting ATM users through a coordinated distraction technique. “One member observes the victim entering their PIN and identifies the bank card, while another creates a distraction. The victim’s card is then swapped, allowing the suspects to use the captured card and PIN to access the victim’s funds,” he stated.
